title: Effective C: An Introduction to Professional C Programming
access: Held licensed edition; paid print/e-book; publisher sample chapter
reason: Held C textbook supplies the object and string contracts used to explain the first invalid state.
locators: Allocating Memory Without Declaring a Type
assignment_scope: Only the substantive inspected passages identified by locators and inspection.scope; wider topic/contents coverage is discovery evidence, not an inspected reading assignment.

inspection.method: Actual bounded primary passages inspected; capture or held ordinary PDF bytes SHA-256 pinned privately
inspection.scope: Exact existing held second-edition payload f1c6; PDF pp.146–158 and 179–188, printed pp. 116–128 and 149–158. Actual malloc/calloc, nonzero realloc, free/dangling, NUL/extent and selected caller-validation text inspected.
inspection.limits: Publication year 2024 follows publisher release; held copyright 2025 is separate. Only named bounded passages; no complete chapter or Annex K availability claim. Portable drills exclude zero-size realloc and C23-only deallocation APIs. Nulling one owner does not repair aliases. No copied book solutions.

title: AddressSanitizer
reason: Defines the address/lifetime detector experiment and its build, resource and platform limits.
prerequisites: C object lifetime, extents and error contracts

inspection.method: Actual bounded primary passages inspected; capture or held ordinary PDF bytes SHA-256 pinned privately
inspection.scope: Actual introduction, compile/link and symbolizer paragraphs, first-error policy, use-after-return mode discussion, leak-detection platform notes, resource limits and supported-platform list.
inspection.limits: Supported does not mean installed or observed. Windows has weaker port support. ASan changes allocation and stack usage; its native resource bound is not the production bound. Not a general uninitialized-value checker, ownership proof or Cortex-M firmware runtime.

title: MemorySanitizer
reason: Contrasts initialization-use tracking with ASan addressability, including an explicit coverage prerequisite.
prerequisites: C object lifetime, extents and error contracts

inspection.method: Actual bounded primary passages inspected; capture or held ordinary PDF bytes SHA-256 pinned privately
inspection.scope: Actual branch/pointer/parameter-use examples, compile/link instructions, origin levels, external-code instrumentation requirement and interceptors, supported OS and resource/link limits.
inspection.limits: Supplemental experiment only on a supported, correctly instrumented setup. Linux/NetBSD/FreeBSD scope; no Windows claim. Uninstrumented dependencies can invalidate interpretation. Not a mandatory replacement for the supported Memcheck comparison.

title: UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer
reason: Separates language undefined behavior checks from defined unsigned size wrap and contract rejection.
prerequisites: C object lifetime, extents and error contracts

inspection.method: Actual bounded primary passages inspected; capture or held ordinary PDF bytes SHA-256 pinned privately
inspection.scope: Actual selected signed-overflow/alignment/bounds checks, recover/trap setup, the undefined group exclusions, unsigned-overflow check and stack-trace prerequisites.
inspection.limits: Default undefined group excludes unsigned overflow, local-bounds and implicit conversions. An optional unsigned-overflow diagnostic does not make unsigned wrapping undefined C behavior. Selected checks only; not every memory bug is covered.

title: LeakSanitizer
reason: Supports a separately declared end-of-process lost-allocation observation.
prerequisites: C object lifetime, extents and error contracts

inspection.method: Actual bounded primary passages inspected; capture or held ordinary PDF bytes SHA-256 pinned privately
inspection.scope: Actual delayed leak phase, ASan integration versus standalone compile/link usage and supported platforms.
inspection.limits: Detection settings, roots and platform affect results. A retained reachable allocation and excessive retained bytes need their own ownership/resource contract. Native RSS or a missing leak report is not the oracle.

title: Memcheck: a memory error detector
reason: Provides the separate unsanitized supported-host comparison for value state, invalid release and leak reachability.
prerequisites: C object lifetime, extents and error contracts

inspection.method: Actual bounded primary passages inspected; capture or held ordinary PDF bytes SHA-256 pinned privately
inspection.scope: Manual identity confirmed at manual index. Actual 4.1/4.2.1–2/4.2.4/4.2.10 and bounded 4.5.1–2 read: addressability versus value propagation, observable-use reporting, root/start/interior classification and leak-error policy.
inspection.limits: Current HTML snapshot pinned by hash; version identity from index. Conservative machine-level roots can differ from the original finite object graph. Addressable stack/global storage need not preserve C subobject bounds. Reports do not identify the moment a handle was lost. Supported Linux comparison must be run separately from ASan-instrumented binaries.

title: AddressSanitizer: A Fast Address Sanity Checker
access: Public author paper via conference publisher
reason: Explains shadow/redzone/quarantine mechanisms and why observing no error cannot establish complete bounds or lifetime safety.

inspection.method: Actual bounded primary passages inspected; capture or held ordinary PDF bytes SHA-256 pinned privately
inspection.scope: Actual PDF pp. 3–4, selected section 3.1–3.5 algorithm and false-negative passages. Title/authors verified; no benchmark reproduction.
inspection.limits: Historical implementation, not a present platform/overhead prediction. The paper describes misses after memory reuse and accesses reaching another valid allocation; current tool behavior must be observed independently. C++ illustrations are conceptual evidence, not C starter code.

title: Using the GNU Compiler Collection
reason: Supplies version-specific frame qualifiers for a closed call-path/nesting calculation.

inspection.method: Actual bounded primary passages inspected; capture or held ordinary PDF bytes SHA-256 pinned privately
inspection.scope: Actual GCC 15.2 Developer Options entries: three .su fields, static/dynamic/bounded meanings, su callgraph marker and LTO-output caveat.
inspection.limits: Per-function report alone is not a complete system bound. Dynamic without bounded gives only a bounded portion; indirect callees, recursion, ABI/interrupt frames and target optimizations need explicit assumptions. GCC development manual has a different field layout, so it is not substituted.

title: GCC program instrumentation options, selected verification and hardening contracts
reason: Distinguishes guard checks and OS/runtime probing from stack-capacity and object-lifetime proofs.

inspection.method: Actual bounded primary passages inspected; capture or held ordinary PDF bytes SHA-256 pinned privately
inspection.scope: Actual selected guard-entry/exit and optimized-away-variable rules, stronger selection, stack-check runtime dependence and target-limited page-probing text.
inspection.limits: No generic bare-metal flag recipe. Hardening and instrumented dependency/resource changes are audited separately. A stack canary need not detect every write or stack exhaustion.

title: Using LD, the GNU linker
reason: Separates fixed region capacity, load/run placement, startup actions and explicit stack reservation.

inspection.method: Actual bounded primary passages inspected; capture or held ordinary PDF bytes SHA-256 pinned privately
inspection.scope: Actual complete short MEMORY and LMA pages; ASSERT paragraphs including provided-symbol evaluation order; selected map/region-report option paragraphs. MEMORY declares fixed regions, does not shuffle sections; startup example copies initialized data and zeros .bss.
inspection.limits: Versioned linker semantics, not a CPU/allocator layout guarantee. Region usage is link placement, not dynamic heap or worst-case stack measurement. A deliberate custom heap/stack collision exists only under the stated synthetic map; ordinary hosted heaps need not share a growing interval.

inspection.method: Actual bounded primary passages inspected; capture or held ordinary PDF bytes SHA-256 pinned privately
inspection.scope: Actual current manual index identity and complete watchpoint page: hardware/software choice, expression versus location, width/count limits, out-of-scope removal, read/access watches and multithread software limits.
inspection.limits: Shared identity coordinated with T44 author. Development snapshot is not installed/released-version authority. title: getrlimit(2) — resource-limit interface
reason: Supports a child-only bounded Linux stack-exhaustion experiment with verified limit setup.
locators: DESCRIPTION — soft and hard limits; RLIMIT_CORE, RLIMIT_CPU and RLIMIT_STACK
NOTES — inheritance across fork and exec

inspection.method: Actual bounded primary passages inspected; capture or held ordinary PDF bytes SHA-256 pinned privately
inspection.scope: Actual soft/hard permission paragraphs, core/CPU/stack entries, return/error text and inherited per-process limits; colophon identifies tarball 6.19.
inspection.limits: Linux process-stack scope, not each pthread stack or bare metal. A handler on an exhausted stack requires a separate signal stack; this drill instead lets the supervisor collect termination. Sanitizer virtual mappings can conflict with generic address-space limits. Learner must read back actual child limits; setup failure is not successful exhaustion.
